senses.definition: To introduce (something) as a reasoned conclusion; to conclude by reasoning or deduction, as from premises or evidence.
senses.example: It is dangerous to infer too much from martial bluster in British politics: at the first hint of trouble, channelling Churchill is a default tactic for beleaguered leaders of all sorts.

senses.definition: To lead to (something) as a consequence; to imply.
senses.example:
a. 1535, Thomas More, letter to Fryth
the fyrste parte is not the proofe of the second. but rather contrarywyse the seconde inferreth well yͤ fyrst.

senses.definition: To cause, inflict (something) upon or to someone.
senses.example: faire Serena[…]fled fast away, afeard / Of villany to be to her inferd[…].

senses.definition: To introduce (a subject) in speaking, writing etc.; to bring in, to adduce.
senses.example: Full well hath Clifford played the orator, / Inferring arguments of mighty force.
